main.title: The Bread That Is Also the Plate
main.clueText: A spongy, slightly sour flatbread made from a tiny gluten-free grain is used as plate, spoon and side dish all at once. Where is it from?
hints: The batter ferments for several days and is cooked on a large round clay griddle.
Its grain is one of the smallest cereal grains in the world.
Diners tear off pieces with the right hand to scoop up stews called wat or tsebhi.
main.answerExplanation: Injera is a fermented flatbread made mainly from teff flour. It is the foundation of everyday meals in Ethiopia and Eritrea, where stews are served on top of a large round of injera.
main.culturalSignificance: Eating from a shared platter is a sign of togetherness. Gursha — lovingly placing a mouthful into someone else’s mouth — is a gesture of hospitality and affection.
main.surprisingFact: Teff is one of the world’s smallest cereal grains — a single grain is often under 1 mm long.
main.originNuance: Injera belongs to both Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine, so both are accepted. Related flatbreads such as canjeero/lahoh are eaten in Somalia, Djibouti and Yemen.
